Rashi on Shabbat 143a:11:1.english: Pits - Of dates, and they are [used] for animal [feed].

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:11:2.hebrew: ארמייתא - תמרים רעים הם, ומאכילין התמרים עצמן לבהמה. הלכך, אגב אימייהו לבהמה נמי קיימי:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:11:2.english: Aramean - They are inferior dates, and people feed the dates themselves to animals. Therefore, along with their mother [the dates], [the pits] also stand [designated] for animals.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:11:3.english: Persian [dates] - They are good dates, and one does not feed them to animals.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:12:1.hebrew: כל צרכו - משתמש בו, ואין כאן משום בזיון, וממחהו בתבשיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:12:1.english: All his needs - He uses it, and there is no [issue] here on account of disgrace [to the bread], and [afterward] he dissolves it in a cooked dish.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:13:1.english: A pitcher of water - A basin of water.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:13:2.hebrew: גרף של ריעי - צוברן לפניו כשאוכל התמרים עד שנמאסות בעיניו, ונוטלן אותן מפניו כגרף של ריעי, ונותנן לבהמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:13:2.english: A chamber pot with excrement - He piles them up in front of him when he eats the dates until they become repulsive in his eyes, and he removes them from before him like a chamber pot with excrement, and gives them to an animal.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:14:1.hebrew: זריק להו בלישני' - אל עבר השלחן:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:14:1.english: He would throw them with his tongue - Toward the other side of the table.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:14:2.english: Behind the bed - upon which he reclines.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:1:1.hebrew: התם כיון דמסרח - מעייא, אי מצנע ליה עד אורתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:1:1.english: There, since it will putrefy - [namely,] the intestines, if he puts it away until evening.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:1:2.hebrew: מאתמול דעתיה עליה - לשונרא, ובין השמשות נמי מוכן לבהמה הוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:1:2.english: From yesterday his mind is upon it - [Intended] for the cat, and at twilight as well it was prepared for an animal.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:1.hebrew: אוד - פורגו"ן, דסתם עצים להסקה ניתנו ולא לטלטול כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:1.english: A poker - [Old French:] forgon [a fire poker]; for ordinary wood is designated for kindling, and not for moving [as] a utensil.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:2.english: And a poker that broke - [That is, it broke] on the Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:3.hebrew: בשברי כלים - שנשברו היום, דהוו להו נולד:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:3.english: With broken vessels - [Ones] that broke today, for they have become nolad [an item newly formed on the Festival].

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:4.hebrew: ש"מ - דכרבי יהודה סבירא ליה, דאית ליה מוקצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:2:4.english: Conclude from it - that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who holds [the principle of] muktzeh.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:1.english: One may clear - with [one's] hands from the table.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:2.english: Bones - hard [ones] that are not fit for a dog.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:3.hebrew: וקליפין - של אגוזים, דלית להו לב"ש מוקצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:3.english: And shells - Of nuts, for Beit Shammai do not hold of [the prohibition of] muktzeh.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:4.hebrew: וב"ה אומרים מסלק את הטבלא - שיש תורת כלי עליה, אבל לא יטלטל הקליפין בידים, כרבי יהודה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:3:4.english: And Beit Hillel say: One removes the board - For it has the status of a vessel, but he may not move the shells with [his] hands, in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:4:1.english: One may clear from the table - It is an unattributed [Mishnah].

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:4:2.hebrew: פירורין פחות מכזית - וכ"ש כזית, כדמפרש טעמא שהם מאכל בהמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:4:2.english: Crumbs less than an olive-bulk - And all the more so [crumbs of] an olive-bulk, as [the Mishnah] explains the reason, that they are animal food.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:4:3.english: And pea pods [lit., hair of peas] - [These are] the pods of legumes in which the legumes grow.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:4:4.english: Peas - [In Old French,] jesses [chickling vetch / grass peas].

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:5:1.english: Leather [as] a handle - [A handle] of leather by which one may hold it.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:5:2.english: One may wipe with it - [The] table.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:5:3.english: One may not wipe with it - For when one holds it, it is squeezed between his fingers.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:5:4.english: May be moved on Shabbat - When it is dry.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:5:5.english: And it does not become ritually impure - For it is neither a wooden vessel, nor a garment, nor sackcloth, nor metal.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:6:1.hebrew: אנו אין לנו - אין אנו סומכין על משנתינו כמות שהיא שנויה, אלא מוחלפת שיטתה, וב"ש כרבי יהודה כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:6:1.english: We have only - We do not rely upon our Mishnah as it is taught; rather, its positions are reversed, and Beit Shammai [hold] like Rabbi Yehuda, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:7:1.english: It is prohibited to destroy them by hand - [This is inferred] from [the fact] that [the Mishnah] teaches "one clears [them] away" with [one's] hands, and does not throw them.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:8:1.hebrew: דלית ליה מוקצה - דאי ר' יהודה, מאתמול לאו לבהמה קיימי, שהרי האוכל היה עמהן, והיום לוקח מהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 143a:8:1.english: Who does not hold of muktzeh - For if [it were] Rabbi Yehuda, from yesterday [before Shabbat] they did not stand [designated] for animal [fodder], since the food was with them, and today he takes [the food] from them.

Rashi on Shabbat 143a:9:1.english: That is unintentional - That he does not intend to squeeze [it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:12:1.hebrew: שמואל מטלטל להו אגב ריפתא - אף על גב דכר"ש סבירא ליה, דשרי לקמן בפרק בתרא (שבת דף קנו:) נבלה שנתנבלה בשבת — מיהו מחמיר היה, משום דהוה אדם חשוב, כאביי ורבא דלעיל. ר"ת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:12:1.english: Shmuel would carry them along with bread - Even though he holds like Rabbi Shimon, who permits below in the last chapter (Shabbat 156b) [handling] a carcass that died on Shabbat, nevertheless he was stringent because he was an important person, like Abaye and Rava [mentioned] above. Rabbeinu Tam.

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:13:1.hebrew: רבא מטלטל להו אגב לקנא דמיא - ואם תאמר: והא רבא סבר לעיל כר"י דאית ליה מוקצה, ואנוחי לקנא דמיא היכי שרי לכתחילה? ויש לומר: דשני לן בין היכא דאפשר למיעבד האי טלטול מאתמול להיכא דלא אפשר; דכיפין ובר יונה היו מאתמול בידו והיה יכול לטלטלם, אבל הני גרעיני תמרה לא אפשר, ושרי אפילו לרבי יהודה ואף לאדם חשוב. דאמר בביצה פרק יו"ט (ביצה דף כא:), דאמר ליה אביי לרב יוסף: הני סופלי לחיותא היכי שדינן ביומא טבא לרבי יוסי דאמר "לכם" ולא לכלבים? חזיין להסקה כו'. בשבת מאי איכא למימר? מטלטלין להו אגב ריפתא כדשמואל. אלמא דאפילו רב יוסף, דלא בעי למישרי לעיל אגב כפא וסכינא אפילו דבר הראוי לאדם, שרי התם גרעיני תמרה אגב ריפתא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:13:1.english: Rava would move them along with a pitcher of water - And if you will say: But Rava holds earlier like Rabbi Yehudah, who maintains [the prohibition of] muktzeh, so how is setting down a pitcher of water [to move them] permitted ab initio? And one can answer that we distinguish between a case where it was possible to do this moving from yesterday [before Shabbat] and a case where it was not possible; for the sheaves and the young pigeon were in his possession from yesterday and he could have moved them [then], whereas [with] these date pits it was not possible, and [therefore] it is permitted even according to Rabbi Yehudah and even for an important person. For it is stated in Beitzah, in the chapter [entitled] Yom Tov (Beitzah 21b), where Abaye said to Rav Yosef: "How may we throw these date pits to the animals on a festival according to Rabbi Yosei, who says [that the verse states] 'for you' — and not for dogs?" [Rav Yosef replied:] "They are fit for kindling, etc." [Abaye asked:] "On Shabbat, what is there to say?" [Rav Yosef replied:] "One may move them along with bread, in accordance with Shmuel." Thus [we see] that even Rav Yosef — who did not want to permit earlier [moving] even something fit for a person along with a ladle or a knife — permits there [moving] date pits along with bread.

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:1:1.hebrew: התם כיון דמסרח - ומתקלקל ואין ראוי למאכל אדם, מאתמול דעתיה עילויה ליתנו לבהמה. אע"ג דבשער של אפונין ושל עדשים אסרינן לרבי יהודה, אע"ג דחזו למאכל בהמה, וכן גרעינין דלעיל בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כט.) דאמרינן לרבי יהודה: "אכלן, אין מסיקין בגרעינן" — מ"מ הכא שרי, כדפי' התם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:1:1.english: There, since it will putrefy - and spoil and is not fit for human consumption, from yesterday [before Shabbat] his mind is set upon it to give it to an animal. Even though regarding stalks of peas and lentils we prohibit [moving them] according to Rabbi Yehuda, even though they are fit for animal consumption, and similarly [regarding] pits above in the chapter Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 29a), where we say according to Rabbi Yehuda: "[If] one ate them, one may not kindle [a fire] with the pits" — nevertheless, here it is permitted, as we explained there.

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:2:1.hebrew: ליטול מהן אוד - נראה לר"ת כפירוש ה"ג דאסירי משום תיקוני מנא, דלפירו' זה דאע"ג דלא מתקצא ליה, גזרינן שלא יבא לידי תיקון כלי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:2:1.english: To take a poker from them - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam in accordance with the explanation of Halakhot Gedolot, that they are prohibited because of fashioning a vessel; for according to this explanation, even though it is not set aside [muktzeh] for him, we enact a decree lest he come to fashion a vessel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:3:1.hebrew: עצמות וקליפין - לא כפירוש הקונטרס, דפירש אפילו קשין ואין ראויין לאכילת כלבים. דהאי תנא, אמרינן בגמרא דכרבי שמעון סבירא ליה, ור"ש בעי לכל הפחות ראויות למאכל בהמה — דקתני: "מעבירין מעל השלחן פירורין כו', מפני שהוא מאכל בהמה", ומוקמינן בגמרא כוותיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:3:1.english: Bones and shells - Not like the explanation of Rashi, who explained [that this refers] even [to] hard ones that are not fit for dogs' consumption. For [regarding] this Tanna, we say in the Gemara that he holds like Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Shimon requires [that they be] at least fit for animal consumption — as it teaches: "One may clear from the table crumbs, etc., because it is animal food," and we establish [the Mishnah] in the Gemara in accordance with him:

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:6:1.hebrew: אנו אין לנו אלא ב"ש כר"י כו' - במסכת עדיות לא מיתניא בהדי קולי ב"ש וחומרי ב"ה, והיינו כרב נחמן. והא דלא מייתי סייעתא מהתם, משום דמאי אולמא דהא מהא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:6:1.english: "We have only Beit Shammai in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, etc." - In Tractate Eduyot, [this dispute] is not taught among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel, and this accords with Rav Nachman. And the reason [the Gemara] does not bring support from there is because what is the strength of this [Mishnah] over that [one]?

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:7:1.hebrew: פירורין שאין בהן כזית אסור לאבדן ביד - פי' בקונט': מדקתני "מעבירין", ולא קתני "זורקין". וקשה לרבי: דברישא נמי קתני "מגביהין מעל השלחן עצמות וקליפין", ולא קתני "זורקין", אע"פ שמותר לאבדן ביד! ועוד, דאמרינן בברכות בריש אלו דברים (ברכות דף נב:): "וב"ה אומרים: אם שמש ת"ח הוא, נוטל פירורין שיש בהן כזית, ומניח פירורין שאין בהן כזית; ומסייע ליה לר' יוחנן, דאמר: פירורין שאין בהן כזית מותר לאבדן ביד", ואי אפשר ליגרס התם "אסור". ונראה לר' דהכא גרסי' "מותר". ודייק מדאצטריך למיתני "מפני שהוא מאכל בהמה", דהיינו משמע דלא חזי לאדם והוו כשאר מאכל בהמה, ומותר לאבדן. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:7:1.english: "Crumbs that are less than an olive-bulk, it is prohibited to destroy them by hand" - Rashi explained [that this is inferred] from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "one clears away" and does not teach "one throws away." And this is difficult for the Rabbi: for in the first clause [of the Mishnah] as well, it teaches "one lifts from the table bones and peels," and it does not teach "one throws away," even though it is permitted to destroy them by hand! And furthermore, we say in Berakhot at the beginning of [the chapter] Eilu Devarim (Berakhot 52b): "And Beit Hillel say: If the waiter is a Torah scholar, he takes the crumbs that are an olive-bulk and leaves the crumbs that are less than an olive-bulk; and this supports Rabbi Yochanan, who said: Crumbs that are less than an olive-bulk, it is permitted to destroy them by hand," and it is impossible to read [the text] there as "it is prohibited." Rather, it appears to the Rabbi that here [too] we read "it is permitted." And [the Gemara] infers this from the fact that [the Mishnah] needed to teach "because it is animal food" — which implies that they are not fit for human [consumption], and they are like other animal food, and it is permitted to destroy them. [From my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:9:1.hebrew: ואם לאו אין מקנחין בו - אית ספרים דגרסי: "וחכ"א: בין כך ובין כך מקנחין בו". ולא יתכן, דאמר בגמרא דבאין לו עור בית אחיזה אפילו ר"ש מודה דאסור, משום דפסיק רישיה הוא. וה"ר יצחק מדנפירא גרס: "בין כך ובין כך אין מקנחין בו", כרבי יהודה דאמר: דבר שאין מתכוין אסור. ואין נראה לר"י, דהא בגמרא משמע דברישא מודה ר' יהודה, דאמר: "אימא סיפא: ספוג, אם יש לו עור בית אחיזה — מקנחין בו, ואם לאו — אין מקנחין בו, אתאן לרבי יהודה". אם כן, "בין כך ובין כך אין מקנחין בו" — לא רבי יהודה ולא ר' שמעון; אלא ודאי לא גרסינן ליה כלל. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 143a:9:1.english: And if not, one may not wipe with it - There are books that read: "And the Sages say: Either way, one may wipe with it." But [this] is not plausible, for [the Gemara] states that when it does not have a leather handle, even Rabbi Shimon agrees that it is prohibited, because it is an inevitable consequence. And Rabbi Yitzchak of Dampierre reads: "Either way, one may not wipe with it," in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, who says: An unintentional act is prohibited. However, [this] does not appear [correct] to the Ri, for in the Gemara it is implied that in the first clause Rabbi Yehudah agrees, as [the Gemara] says: "Say the latter clause: A sponge, if it has a leather handle — one may wipe with it, and if not — one may not wipe with it; we have arrived at [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehudah." If so, [the reading] "either way, one may not wipe with it" [is held by] neither Rabbi Yehudah nor Rabbi Shimon; rather, we certainly do not read it at all. M.R.:
